This document uses data coming from the following article:

- Feng, S.F., Wang, S., Zarnescu, S. et al. The dynamics of explore–exploit decisions reveal a signal-to-noise mechanism for random exploration. Sci Rep 11, 3077 (2021). Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-82530-8


We aim to replicate some of the figures and analysis from the paper in order to get some insights for a new project (e.g. required sample size, amount of trials)

This chunk should imitate the function in `load_humanData_v1.m`

```{r data_loading}
#### 1. Load horizon and demographic data ####
# the original code loaded "allHorizonData_v2.csv", but it was not found in the repo.
# so "allHorizonData_cut.csv" is used instead

complete_data <- read_csv("feng_et_al_2021/repo_files/allHorizonData_cut.csv")
demographic_data <- read_csv("feng_et_al_2021/repo_files/DDM_demographics.csv")

#### 2. Apply original data processing steps ####
clean_data <- complete_data %>%
  
  # princeton subjects only
  filter(expt_name %in% c('pilot-v1', 'repeater-v1')) %>%
  
  # align some notations for later on
  mutate(sID = "sNum") %>%
  
  #  load demographics
  left_join(demographic_data, by = c("subjectID" = "fname")) %>%
  
  # remove fast or slow RTs
  # Here, the original script pointed to "a" as the response variable.
  # but it was absent in the data so I suppose I should use "c". ("C_5", actually)
  mutate(
    c5 = ifelse(rt5 > 0.1 & rt5 < 3, c5, NA)
  ) %>% 

# 3. Count excluded trials per subject

  mutate(nExcluded = sum(is.na(c5)), .by = "subjectID")
```

# 2. Report demographics and exclude subjects

This is a bit different from the original code. The original dataset from the repo does not include the "excluded" variable. Maybe it's in the `allHorizonData_v2.csv` file (which I didn't find).

I applied the exclusion criteria stated in the paper (include only subjects with at least 131 trials per horizon condition).

```{r}

 df %>%
  # group_by(subjectID, gameLength) %>% 
  mutate(nIncluded = sum(!is.na(c5)), .by = c("subjectID", "gameLength"))  %>% 
  mutate(Include = ifelse(nIncluded >= 132, 1, 0)) %>% 
  mutate(Include_subject = min(Include),.by = "subjectID") %>% 
  filter(Include_subject == 1) %>% 
  distinct(subjectID, is_male, age) %>% 
  summarise(total = n(),
            male = sum(is_male, na.rm=TRUE),
            female = sum(!is_male, na.rm=TRUE),
            min_age = min(age, na.rm=TRUE),
            max_age = max(age, na.rm=TRUE),
            mean_age = mean(age, na.rm=TRUE))


clean_data <- clean_data %>% 
  mutate(nIncluded = sum(!is.na(c5)), .by = c("subjectID", "gameLength"))  %>% 
  mutate(Include = ifelse(nIncluded >= 132, 1, 0))%>% 
  mutate(Include_subject = min(Include),.by = "subjectID") %>% 
  filter(Include_subject == 1)
```

```{r}

# Funciones auxiliares de verosimilitud
lik_13 <- function(X, dm, c5, uc, priorFlag) {
  bias <- X[1]
  sigma <- X[2]
  bonus <- X[3]
  
  if (is.na(sigma) || is.na(bias) || is.na(bonus)) return(Inf)
  if (sigma <= 0) return(Inf) # Prevenir división por cero o valores negativos
  
  dQ <- dm + uc * bonus + bias
  P <- 1 / (1 + exp(-1 / (sigma * sqrt(2)) * dQ))
  
  # Evitar log(0)
  P <- pmin(pmax(P, 1e-15), 1 - 1e-15)
  
  lP1 <- log(P[c5 == 1 & !is.na(c5)])
  lP0 <- log(1 - P[c5 == 0 & !is.na(c5)])
  
  if (priorFlag) {
    # Equivalente a gaussianPrior(bonus, 0, 20) y exponentialPrior(sigma, 1/20)
    L_AB <- dnorm(bonus, mean = 0, sd = 20, log = TRUE)
    L_noise <- dexp(sigma, rate = 1/20, log = TRUE)
    LL <- -(sum(lP1) + sum(lP0) + L_AB + L_noise)
  } else {
    LL <- -(sum(lP1) + sum(lP0))
  }
  return(LL)
}

lik_22 <- function(X, dm, c5, priorFlag) {
  bias <- X[1]
  sigma <- X[2]
  
  if (is.na(sigma) || is.na(bias)) return(Inf)
  if (sigma <= 0) return(Inf)
  
  dQ <- dm + bias
  P <- 1 / (1 + exp(-1 / (sigma * sqrt(2)) * dQ))
  
  # Evitar log(0)
  P <- pmin(pmax(P, 1e-15), 1 - 1e-15)
  
  lP1 <- log(P[c5 == 1 & !is.na(c5)])
  lP0 <- log(1 - P[c5 == 0 & !is.na(c5)])
  
  if (priorFlag) {
    L_noise <- dexp(sigma, rate = 1/20, log = TRUE)
    LL <- -(sum(lP1) + sum(lP0) + L_noise)
  } else {
    LL <- -(sum(lP1) + sum(lP0))
  }
  return(LL)
}

# Función principal de ajuste
fit_biasNoiseBonus_v2 <- function(sub, priorFlag = FALSE) {
  
  L <- unique(sub$gameLength)
  n_horizons <- length(L)
  
  LL <- numeric(n_horizons)
  k <- numeric(n_horizons)
  n <- numeric(n_horizons)
  
  # Matriz para almacenar parámetros (3 del [1 3] y 2 del [2 2] = 5 filas)
  x_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = 5, ncol = n_horizons)
  
  for (i in seq_along(L)) {
    
    # --- [1 3] condition ---
    # Asumiendo que sub$n1_4, sub$a_5, etc., son vectores extraídos previamente de las matrices
    ind13 <- (sub$gameLength == L[i]) & (sub$n1_4 != sub$n2_4) & (!is.na(sub$a_5))
    
    c5 <- sub$a_5[ind13] == 2
    dm <- sub$o2_4[ind13] - sub$o1_4[ind13]
    uc <- -(sub$n2_4[ind13] - sub$n1_4[ind13]) / 2
    
    # Optimización [1 3]: x = [bias, sigma, bonus]
    X0_13 <- c(0, 10, 0)
    LB_13 <- c(-100, 0.001, -100) # sigma no puede ser exactamente 0
    UB_13 <- c(100, 100, 100)
    
    fit13 <- optim(par = X0_13, fn = lik_13, dm = dm, c5 = c5, uc = uc, priorFlag = priorFlag, 
                   method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = LB_13, upper = UB_13)
    
    tar13 <- fit13$value
    x_13 <- fit13$par
    LL[i] <- -tar13
    
    # --- [2 2] condition ---
    ind22 <- (sub$gameLength == L[i]) & (sub$n1_4 == sub$n2_4) & (!is.na(sub$a_5))
    
    c5_22 <- sub$a_5[ind22] == 2
    dm_22 <- sub$o2_4[ind22] - sub$o1_4[ind22]
    # En MATLAB dice sub(1).n2(ind,4), asumo que es para extraer la estructura si es un array
    uc_22 <- (sub$n2_4[ind22] - sub$n1_4[ind22]) / 2 
    
    # Optimización [2 2]: x = [bias, sigma]
    X0_22 <- c(0, 10)
    LB_22 <- c(-100, 0.001)
    UB_22 <- c(100, 100)
    
    fit22 <- optim(par = X0_22, fn = lik_22, dm = dm_22, c5 = c5_22, priorFlag = priorFlag, 
                   method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = LB_22, upper = UB_22)
    
    tar22 <- fit22$value
    x_22 <- fit22$par
    
    LL[i] <- LL[i] - tar22
    k[i] <- length(X0_13) + length(X0_22)
    n[i] <- sum(sub$gameLength == L[i], na.rm = TRUE)
    
    x_matrix[, i] <- c(x_13, x_22)
  }
  
  total_n <- length(sub$n2_4)
  
  BIC_val <- -2 * sum(LL) + sum(k) * log(sum(n))
  LPT_val <- exp(-BIC_val / sum(n) / 2)
  
  AIC_val <- -2 * sum(LL) + sum(k) * 2
  LPTa_val <- exp(-AIC_val / sum(n) / 2)
  
  # Generar funciones anidadas para generar las curvas sigmoides teóricas
  cc13_funcs <- list()
  cc22_funcs <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_len(n_horizons)) {
    # Asegurar evaluación local de los parámetros con force() o evaluando variables
    b13 <- x_matrix[1, i]; s13 <- x_matrix[2, i]; bon13 <- x_matrix[3, i]
    b22 <- x_matrix[4, i]; s22 <- x_matrix[5, i]
    
    cc13_funcs[[i]] <- function(x, bonus=bon13, bias=b13, sigma=s13) {
      1 / (1 + exp(-1 / (sigma * sqrt(2)) * (x + bonus + bias)))
    }
    cc22_funcs[[i]] <- function(x, bias=b22, sigma=s22) {
      1 / (1 + exp(-1 / (sigma * sqrt(2)) * (x + bias)))
    }
  }
  
  # Estructurar resultados de salida similares a un struct
  list(
    model_name = 'original',
    var_names = c('bias13', 'noise13', 'bonus', 'bias22', 'noise22'),
    x = x_matrix,
    bic = BIC_val,
    lpt = LPT_val,
    LL = sum(LL),
    k = sum(k),
    n = sum(n),
    aic = AIC_val,
    lpta = LPTa_val,
    cc13 = cc13_funcs,
    cc22 = cc22_funcs
  )
}

# MLE fits
priorFlag <- 1
fit_logistic <- list() # Store results in a list instead of a struct array

for (sn in seq_along(clean_data)) {
  # fit_biasNoiseBonus_v2 must return a list containing the parameters 
  # and the functional forms for the curves (cc13 and cc22)
  fit_logistic[[sn]] <- fit_biasNoiseBonus_v2(clean_data[1,], priorFlag)
}

# compute model choice curves
x_vals <- seq(-30, 30, by = 0.01)

# Pre-allocate 3D arrays (length of x_vals rows, 2 columns, N subjects "pages")
n_subjects <- length(clean_data)
cc13 <- array(NA, dim = c(length(x_vals), 2, n_subjects))
cc22 <- array(NA, dim = c(length(x_vals), 2, n_subjects))

for (sn in 1:n_subjects) {
  for (i in 1:2) {
    # Assuming cc13[[i]] and cc22[[i]] are functions returned by the fit
    cc13[, i, sn] <- fit_logistic[[sn]]$cc13[[i]](x_vals)
    cc22[, i, sn] <- fit_logistic[[sn]]$cc22[[i]](x_vals)
  }
}

# Calculate the mean across the 3rd dimension (subjects), equivalent to nanmean(..., 3)
CC13 <- apply(cc13, MARGIN = c(1, 2), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
CC22 <- apply(cc22, MARGIN = c(1, 2), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}

# 1. Obtener la lista única de sujetos
sujetos_unicos <- unique(clean_data$subjectID)
n_subjects <- length(sujetos_unicos)

# 2. Bucle para ajustar el modelo por cada sujeto
priorFlag <- 1
fit_logistic <- list()

for (sn in 1:n_subjects) {
  # Filtramos la tabla gigante para quedarnos SOLO con las filas de ESTE sujeto
  datos_un_sujeto <- clean_data %>% 
    filter(subjectID == sujetos_unicos[sn])
  
  # Ahora le pasamos esos datos (que contienen ambos horizontes) a la función.
  # Adentro de la función, unique(sub$gameLength) detectará correctamente los 2 tamaños de juego.
  fit_logistic[[sn]] <- fit_biasNoiseBonus_v2(datos_un_sujeto, priorFlag)
}

# 3. Calcular las curvas de modelo (choice curves)
x_vals <- seq(-30, 30, by = 0.01)

# Pre-asignar los arrays (Filas: x_vals, Columnas: 2 horizontes, "Páginas": N sujetos)
cc13 <- array(NA, dim = c(length(x_vals), 2, n_subjects))
cc22 <- array(NA, dim = c(length(x_vals), 2, n_subjects))

for (sn in 1:n_subjects) {
  
  # Como ahora cada sujeto sí procesó ambos horizontes, la lista de funciones cc13/cc22 tiene 2 elementos
  for (i in 1:2) {
    # i=1 es el primer horizonte (usualmente length 5 / horizon 1)
    # i=2 es el segundo horizonte (usualmente length 10 / horizon 6)
    cc13[, i, sn] <- fit_logistic[[sn]]$cc13[[i]](x_vals)
    cc22[, i, sn] <- fit_logistic[[sn]]$cc22[[i]](x_vals)
  }
}

# 4. Calcular el promedio de las curvas a través de todos los sujetos (dimensión 3)
CC13 <- apply(cc13, MARGIN = c(1, 2), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
CC22 <- apply(cc22, MARGIN = c(1, 2), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# 2. Top Panels: Choice Curves
plot_choice_curve <- function(theoretical_data, title_text, x_label, y_label) {
  # theoretical_data is assumed to be a data frame with columns: x, H1, H6
  ggplot(theoretical_data, aes(x = x)) +
    # Theoretical lines
    geom_line(aes(y = H1, color = "horizon 1"), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_line(aes(y = H6, color = "horizon 6"), linewidth = 1) +
    # Note: To add the empirical binned dots here, you would use geom_point() 
    # fed by clean_data %>% group_by(horizon, reward_diff_bin) %>% summarise(p = mean(choice==2))
    scale_color_manual(values = c("horizon 1" = AZblue, "horizon 6" = AZred)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-35, 35), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = title_text, x = x_label, y = y_label, color = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "plain"), legend.position = "none")
}

# Assuming df_CC13 and df_CC22 are data frames built from your CC13/CC22 matrix averages
p1 <- plot_choice_curve(df_CC13, "unequal [1 3]", "difference in mean reward\nR(high info) - R(low info)", "p(high info)") +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.2)) # 'southeast'
p2 <- plot_choice_curve(df_CC22, "equal [2 2]", "difference in mean reward\nR(left) - R(right)", "p(left)")

# 3. Bottom Panels: Parameter Distributions & T-Tests
plot_param_slope <- function(param_matrix, title_text, y_label, y_limits, bracket_y, text_y) {
  
  # Convert 2xN matrix to long format and calculate explicit jitter to align lines and dots
  df <- as.data.frame(t(param_matrix)) %>%
    rename(H1 = V1, H6 = V2) %>%
    mutate(
      sujeto = row_number(),
      jitter_H1 = 1 + runif(n(), -0.125, 0.125),
      jitter_H6 = 2 + runif(n(), -0.125, 0.125)
    )
  
  # Run Paired T-test
  stats <- t.test(df$H6, df$H1, paired = TRUE)
  p_val <- stats$p.value
  asterisks <- if (p_val < 0.001) "***" else if (p_val < 0.005) "**" else if (p_val < 0.01) "*" else ""
  
  # Print stats to console
  cat(sprintf('%s: t(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %.2e\n', title_text, stats$parameter, stats$statistic, p_val))
  
  # Build plot
  p <- ggplot(df) +
    # Connect subjects with gray lines using explicit jitter coordinates
    geom_segment(aes(x = jitter_H1, xend = jitter_H6, y = H1, yend = H6), color = "gray75", linewidth = 0.5) +
    # Plot points
    geom_point(aes(x = jitter_H1, y = H1), color = AZblue, size = 2) +
    geom_point(aes(x = jitter_H6, y = H6), color = AZred, size = 2) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2), labels = c("1", "6"), limits = c(0.5, 2.5)) +
    labs(title = title_text, x = "horizon", y = y_label) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "plain"))
  
  # Add significance brackets if p < 0.01
  if (asterisks != "") {
    p <- p + 
      annotate("segment", x = 1, xend = 1, y = bracket_y[1], yend = bracket_y[2]) +
      annotate("segment", x = 1, xend = 2, y = bracket_y[2], yend = bracket_y[2]) +
      annotate("segment", x = 2, xend = 2, y = bracket_y[2], yend = bracket_y[3]) +
      annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = text_y, label = asterisks, size = 8)
  }
  
  return(p)
}

p3 <- plot_param_slope(bonus_mat, "directed [1 3]", "information bonus", c(-40, 60), c(15, 50, 45), 52)
p4 <- plot_param_slope(noise13_mat, "random [1 3]", "decision noise", c(0, 50), c(33, 45, 35), 46)
p5 <- plot_param_slope(noise22_mat, "random [2 2]", "decision noise", c(0, 50), c(32, 45, 40), 46)

# 4. Assemble the layout using patchwork
figure_3 <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4 | p5) + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(1.5, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A') # Automatically adds A, B, C, D, E labels

# Display the figure
print(figure_3)
```

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Definir los límites y centros de los intervalos (bins)
bin_edges <- seq(-25, 25, by = 10)
bin_mids <- seq(-20, 20, by = 10)

# 2. Calcular los datos empíricos agrupados (Equivalente al bucle y binIt)
empirical_summary <- clean_data %>%
  filter(rt5 > 0.1 & rt5 < 3) %>%
  mutate(
    dR = o2_4 - o1_4,
    dI = (n2_4 - n1_4) / 2,
    horizon = ifelse(gameLength == 5, "H1", "H6"),
    cond = ifelse(n1_4 == n2_4, "22", "13"),
    
    # Identificar opción de alta información (1 o 2)
    uID = case_when(dI > 0 ~ 1, dI < 0 ~ 2, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    
    # Ejes X e Y adaptados por condición
    x_val = ifelse(cond == "13", -dI * dR, dR),
    y_val = ifelse(cond == "13", as.numeric(a_5 == uID), as.numeric(a_5 == 2)),
    
    # Asignar cada ensayo a su bin correspondiente
    x_bin = as.numeric(as.character(cut(x_val, breaks = bin_edges, labels = bin_mids)))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x_bin)) %>%
  # Promedio por sujeto por bin
  group_by(cond, horizon, x_bin, subjectID) %>%
  summarise(subj_mean = mean(y_val, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  # Promedio y Error Estándar a nivel grupal
  group_by(cond, horizon, x_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    p_mean = mean(subj_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_se = sd(subj_mean, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Extraer los data frames empíricos por condición
emp_13 <- empirical_summary %>% filter(cond == "13")
emp_22 <- empirical_summary %>% filter(cond == "22")

# 3. Función de ploteo actualizada para incluir las curvas teóricas Y los puntos empíricos
plot_choice_curve_combined <- function(df_teorico, df_empirico, title_text, x_label, y_label) {
  
  ggplot() +
    # Puntos empíricos y barras de error
    geom_errorbar(data = df_empirico, 
                  aes(x = x_bin, ymin = p_mean - p_se, ymax = p_mean + p_se, color = horizon), 
                  width = 0, size = 1) +
    geom_point(data = df_empirico, 
               aes(x = x_bin, y = p_mean, color = horizon), 
               size = 4) +
    
    # Curvas teóricas del modelo logístico
    geom_line(data = df_teorico, aes(x = x, y = H1, color = "H1"), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_line(data = df_teorico, aes(x = x, y = H6, color = "H6"), linewidth = 1) +
    
    scale_color_manual(values = c("H1" = AZblue, "H6" = AZred),
                       labels = c("H1" = "horizon 1", "H6" = "horizon 6")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-35, 35), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = title_text, x = x_label, y = y_label, color = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "plain"), legend.position = "none")
}

# 4. Generar los paneles superiores combinados
p1 <- plot_choice_curve_combined(df_CC13, emp_13, "unequal [1 3]", 
                                 "difference in mean reward\nR(high info) - R(low info)", "p(high info)") +
      theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.2)) # Activar leyenda solo en el primer panel

p2 <- plot_choice_curve_combined(df_CC22, emp_22, "equal [2 2]", 
                                 "difference in mean reward\nR(left) - R(right)", "p(left)")
```
